I wrote the round-2 adjudication to /workspace/minlp-notes/paper-open-minlplib/development/reviews/round2/adjudication.md (929 lines). Nothing was committed and no scientific script was run.

**What went in:** 93 numbered review items (sol-referee 9, sol-verify 8, opus-referee 15, opus-consistency 16, opus-writing 31, opus-claims 14) plus the five lead-author decisions LD2-1 to LD2-5. Deduplicated, they give 67 change items and a Build-phase step:

| Group | Items | Major | Minor | Accept | Accept-modified |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | 15 | 5 | 10 | 5 | 10 |
| G2 | 7 | 3 | 4 | 3 | 4 |
| G3 | 9 | 1 | 8 | 6 | 3 |
| G4 | 9 | 3 | 6 | 3 | 6 |
| G5 | 8 | 2 | 6 | 7 | 1 |
| G6 | 10 | 2 | 8 | 5 | 5 |
| G7 | 9 | 1 | 8 | 7 | 2 |
| **Total** | **67** | **17** | **50** | **36** | **31** |

There are no blockers. 17 rejections, each with a reason checked against sources (Section 10); two reject a whole review item (opus-consistency 13 and opus-referee 15), the rest reject parts or options. Every review item maps to a change or a rejection (Section 11). **No certified number changes**: no review proved a display unsafe.

**Page targets (Section 2):**
- **Main text, Sections 1–11:** from 42.85 to 37.3 pages (about 38 once new text is added).
  - G1 9.4 pages, G2 9.7, G3 11.7, G4 6.5.
  - Appendix A stays at or below 3.3 pages; Appendix B goes to 3.0 or less.
- **Supplement body:** from 124.91 to about 105 pages.
  - G5 66 pages (S1 and S5, including a new S1.10).
  - G6 37.0 pages (S2–S4, S6, and its parts of S7 and the former S8).
  - G7 2.2 pages (S7.1 setup and the S7.3 register).
- G5's target is tight. A group that reaches its content floor stops and reports what is indispensable, page by page.

A move table (M1–M15) lists, for each relocated piece, its source location, destination and the groups that remove and insert it, so nothing is lost. The main moves:
- Prop. 4.3(c) and the maximality part of Prop. 4.5, with their proofs, go to a new S1.10.
- Prop. 8.3 and Lemma 8.4 go to S6.6.
- The §1.4 citation list goes to S3.1.
- Table 1 becomes a compact upright table; the full version becomes `tab:trust-full` in S7.2.
- The §11 recommendations join §9 ("Interpretation and recommendations"); §11 becomes "Limitations and conclusion".
- The S8 table goes to `artifact/HISTORY.md`.
- The register's paths and run records go to `artifact/RUNS.md`; the register stays in S7 in a compact form.
- Moved text is taken from the r3 tar (`/workspace/local-home/paper-backups/paper-open-minlplib-r3-20261004-2302.tar`), which I checked is identical to the current sources.

**Decisions to note:**
- **AI disclosure (G1-01, G4-08):** the same wording in §2.6 and the declarations. I added "selected the instances" and "ran the solver experiments and the audit" to the lead author's list, because the records show agents did this (root-research-log, the solver-campaign report, data-semantics.md). The author-confirmation placeholder stays, and no editor writes what a person checked.
- **Tiers:** removed from the §§4–5 certificate sentences; Table 7 (§10) and the certificate boxes keep them. This also fixes the stale waterno2 tier.
- **"Separately written":** the definition now requires that the second session did not read the first code before its own results existed. As a result, `ann_cumene_tanh` has status "proved".
- **IbexOpt:** I checked its documentation (IBEX 2.9, read 2026-10-04). Its rigor mode proves equality-feasible points, and the replacement text and a new bib entry say so.
- **Abstract:** the replacement text has exactly 250 words. It leads with the 79 comparable solver bounds and no longer asserts a public deposit.
- **Artifact recipe (G7-01):** a concrete `mktemp` WORK path with `HOME` set inside WORK, so nothing is written to the real `~/.cache`. A new standard-library script, `prepare_paper_inputs.py`, accepts exactly the 26 documented models the paper does not use.

- **`RELEASE.md` (G7-06):** records the PDF hashes; the Build phase writes them.

**Order of work:** G1–G7 edit in parallel; G7-09 (merging the moved text, rebuilding the index, updating counts) runs after the others finish; then the Build phase runs a single `make`.
